newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian parliament to discuss budget after April 30.
newsitem.headline: Indian parliament to discuss budget after April 30.

text.p: India's parliament will not take up a budget proposal for 1997/98 (April-March) until after April 30, a senior member of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition said on Monday.

Chitta Basu, a member of the All-India Forward Block party, said political parties decided on Monday that parliament would adjourn on Tuesday after a vote of confidence in Gujral, and reassemble on April 30 until May 16.
Basu said the decision was taken at a meeting of parliament's business advisory committee.
"The meeting decided that the house will adjourn tomorrow after discussing the confidence motion. It will reassemble on April 30 and continue to May 16," Basu told Reuters.

Asked if the government would propose the same budget which outgoing finance minister P. Chidambaram unveiled on February 28 before the fall of H.D. Deve Gowda's government, Basu said: "That is for the government to decide."
Human Resource Development Minister S.R. Bommai said Gujral, who kept the finance ministry portfolio for himself, might pilot a budget bill through parliament.
